title: Alert Fatigue Postmortem & Tuning Playbook (draft)
body:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working draft intended to capture recurring causes of pager noise and missing metrics that have led to SLO burn alerts over the last 6 months, plus concrete tuning steps and short runbook stubs on first-response actions. Goal: reduce high-volume, low-signal alerts by 60% in Q1 2025 while keeping worst-case detection windows under current SLO targets.

Quick summary of recent signal: (high level)
- Multiple high-volume pages last quarter got routed to SRE on-call: majority caused by noisy alerts (flapping counters, bad aggregation), not true customer-impacting degradations.
- Several SLO burn pages were triggered during deploy windows and autoscaling events; in some cases the metric series disappeared and the alert fired on a default NA-handling path.
- Two incidents where missing instrumentation (new job / sidecar start) caused downstream alert storms while downstream consumers retried.

Concrete incidents reviewed (representative):
1) 2024-09-19 - embeddings-service: Tokenization latency SLO burn
   - Symptom: SLO error budget consumed > threshold over 10 minutes, on-call received SLO-burn page.
   - Findings: upstream tokenization worker rolling restart exposed a short period where histogram buckets reported 0 and alert rule mistook data absence for 100% error. Alert logic used rate() on a counter that reset during restart.
   - Fixes applied: adjusted rule to use increase() over window and added absent() guard in alert expression. Filed orchestration ticket to include readiness probe dependency map (JIRA-SRE-4124).

2) 2024-10-03 - orchestrator autoscaling noise
   - Symptom: dozens of pages from grouped alert that measured request_5xx_ratio by job label.
   - Findings: Autoscaler triggered pod churn at predicted times; alert threshold not stable against variable sampling windows. Alert used avg_over_time across instance label causing spikes when instance count changed.
   - Fixes applied: moved to sum(rate(...)) / sum(rate(...)) pattern to be resilient to cardinality changes. Added a ‘min_instances’ clause and a temporary suppression during scheduled capacity ramp for known customers.

3) 2024-11-05 - missing metrics after canary deploy
   - Symptom: downstream services paged due to absent KV cache hit metrics; many alerts fired as downstream eval jobs retried.
   - Findings: New canary image introduced a metrics exporter change that renamed metrics. Alerts matched old metric name and returned absent() => fired.
   - Fixes applied: Updated exporter, added metrics compatibility check in CI, added a Prometheus metric existence test into integration pipeline (see linked PR).

Root cause patterns we repeatedly see:
- Metric absence or reset (exporter renames, counter resets on restart) treated as error by alert expressions.
- Aggregation patterns that are sensitive to cardinality changes on scale events (avg over instances vs global sum-rate).
- Thresholds tuned to steady-state traffic and not to deploy windows / scheduled maintenance.
- Overly low severity for common infra noise; lack of priority/owner mapping.
- Missing runbook steps for quick triage of SLO burn alerts (what to check first).

Guiding principles for tuning alerts (short):
- Prefer presence/absence checks earlier in expression: only escalate if metric exists OR if a companion metric indicates downstream errors.
- Use sum(rate(...)) patterns where you care about global percentages across instances, not per-instance averages.
- Guard against counter resets: prefer increase() or handle resets explicitly.
- Add hysteresis: use longer windows for noisy signals, and require sustained violation (e.g., 3/5 windows) before paging.
- Silence rules during known safe windows (deploy windows, scheduled autoscaling) with automatic re-enable.
- Classify alerts: pager (P0/P1), ticket-only (P2), logging-only. Map to escalation policy in OpsgeniePagerDuty.

Runbook stub: SLO-burn alert triage (first 10 minutes)
- Step 0: acknowledge page and annotate incident start time.
- Step 1: check the SLO query in Grafana (open pre-saved dashboard link included in alert). Confirm whether burn is due to increased error rate or missing data.
- Step 2: check metric health: 
    - Use Prometheus: GET /api/v1/series?match[]="<metric_name>" for presence.
    - If absent(), query related exporter uptime metric.
- Step 3: check deploy window / recent rollout: link to releases page and k8s events (kubectl get events --all-namespaces --since=15m).
- Step 4: if metric exists but high errors: check logs for increased 5xx/timeout patterns, run quick flamegraph on service if available.
- Step 5: if metric absent and cause unknown: silence downstream non-critical pages for 10m, triage exporter/sidecar.
- Step 6: communicate: post to #sre-incidents with summary and whether page escalates to product SLAs.

Prometheus rule patterns (examples to standardize):
- Bad pattern we saw: avg_over_time(request_latency_seconds_bucket[1m]) > 0.05
- Prefer pattern: (sum(increase(request_errors_total[5m])) / sum(increase(request_total[5m]))) > 0.05
- Presence guard: (count_values("present", request_total) > 0) and (sum(increase(request_errors_total[5m])) / sum(increase(request_total[5m])) > 0.05)
- Absent handling: absent(up_exporter_up) == 1 -> route to infra-channel but do not auto-trigger SLO burn page unless companion error metric also bad.

Operational controls to implement (action items):
- A1 (owner: Priya) - SLO alert rule review sprint: audit top 25 firing alerts over last 90 days and classify into fix/silence/retune. Target: complete by 2025-01-20. (Linked: CONFLUENCE-9382)
- A2 (owner: Ethan) - Add metric existence tests to CI for all services that supply SLO inputs. Integration gate should fail if critical metrics missing on canary. Target: 2024-12-20. (PR referenced in linked_artifacts)
- A3 (owner: Maya) - Create alert severity taxonomy and map to on-call escalation policies; add documentation and runbook links into alert payloads. Target: 2024-12-15.
- A4 (owner: Liam) - Implement dynamic suppression for known scheduled autoscaler windows and documented maintenance periods. Target: 2025-01-10.
- A5 (owner: Platform) - Add exporter compatibility tests and semantic metric rename policy; require deprecation period. Target: 2025-02-01.

Guidance for on-call (practical heuristics):
- If several pages are all tied to the same metric family or same exporter, start from exporter health.
- If pages fire only during rolling restarts / autoscale, assume cardinality sensitivity and escalate to Platform rather than immediate rollback.
- Avoid immediate paging on absent(): add confirmation via companion metric or manual check unless the alert is tied to critical production paths.

Template alert payload to improve signal: (fields to include in alert body)
- SLO name / exact query used
- Last known good timestamp for metric series
- Link to Grafana panel and runbook stub
- Suggested first-action checklist (3 bullets)
- Service owner contact and escalation policy ID

Open questions and unknowns (work to decide):
- How aggressive should automatic deployment-time suppressions be? risk: silent real regressions during canary. Proposal: only suppress non-pager informational alerts, not SLO-burns tied to customer-facing endpoints.
- Which alerts can be safely downgraded to ticket-only? need product input on tolerance.
- Whether to adopt ML-based anomaly detection for low-volume signals vs more hand-tuned rules.

Notes to reviewers / next steps:
- Review A1 audit list and suggest top 10 candidate alerts to retire or reduce severity.
- Product/Support: confirm tolerance for longer detection windows on non-critical infra metrics.
- Dev teams: add metric-compatibility tests to secondary CI and document any planned renames with deprecation windows.

Appendix: useful commands and queries
- Check series presence: curl -g 'http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/series?match[]=metric_name'
- Quick error rate: sum(increase(http_requests_total{job="X",code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(increase(http_requests_total{job="X"}[5m]))
- Silence creation (opsgenie/pagerduty): link to internal playbook for automatic silences.

This document is iterative. Please annotate with comments or edits; I'll consolidate into the Confluence draft after reviewer signoff.
